newsitem.title: USA: Conrail buy cuts Norfolk's EPS by $0.09/shr.
newsitem.headline: Conrail buy cuts Norfolk's EPS by $0.09/shr.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said Wednesday its Conrail acquisition cut its net earnings by $10.6 million, or $0.09 a share, in the second quarter.
Excluding the charge, the company earned $200.8 million, or $1.61 a share, on $1.30 billion in revenues the second quarter, matching a First Call poll of 13 analysts of $1.61 a share.
This compared with a $199.5 million, or $1.57 a share on revenues of $1.28 billion the year before.
The company said the Conrail charge consisted primarily of expenses related to its buying Conrail stock for an expected total of $5.8 billion.

The company's railway operations posted a record $1.07 billion in revenues in the quarter, up three percent over last year. Its motor carrier operations revenues dropped one percent to $237.2 million over the same period.
Norfolk's railway operating expenses rose one percent to $746.4 million, while its motor carrier operating expenses remained flat at $229.7 million.

The company reported a 16-percent growth in inter-modal revenues, which it ascribed to double-digit volume growth in containers and trailers. It added chemicals led the growth in its general merchandise division, with volume up 10 percent and revenues up seven percent.
Norfolk's stock hit a new 52-week high of 114-5/16 Wednesday morning, and traded later at 113-7/8, up 1-1/8.
